test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 31 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Find the relation between x and y such that the point (x, y) is equidistant from (6, 2) and (4, 6).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The locus of a point **equidistant** from two given points is the **perpendicular bisector** of the segment joining them.

Find the **midpoint** of (6, 2) and (4, 6): M = ((6+4)/2, (2+6)/2) = (5, 4).

Slope of the line joining points (m₁) = (6 − 2) ÷ (4 − 6) = 4 ÷ (−2) = −2.

Slope of **perpendicular bisector** (m₂) = −1 ÷ m₁ = 1/2.

Equation: y − 4 = 1/2 × (x − 5) ⇒ 2y − 8 = x − 5 ⇒ x − 2y = −3.

**∴ The correct answer is x − 2y = −3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Points **A(6, 2)** and **B(4, 6)**. Point **P(x, y)** is equidistant from A and B.

**Formula Used:** Distance between (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e936686f93ba70afd7a88fe13a34614241a67fe2be139e3fa63bce60147553f9.png] 

According to the question, **PA = PB**

⇒ PA² = PB²

⇒ (x − 6)² + (y − 2)² = (x − 4)² + (y − 6)²

⇒ x² − 12x + 36 + y² − 4y + 4 = x² − 8x + 16 + y² − 12y + 36

⇒ −12x − 4y + 40 = −8x − 12y + 52

⇒ −12x + 8x − 4y + 12y = 52 − 40

⇒ −4x + 8y = 12

⇒ −4(x − 2y) = 12

⇒ x − 2y = 12 ÷ (−4)

⇒ x − 2y = −3

**∴ The correct answer is x − 2y = −3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Distance Formula

Used to calculate the distance between two points in a 2D plane: d = √[(x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²].

Perpendicular Bisector

Every point on the perpendicular bisector of a line segment is equidistant from the endpoints of the segment.

Midpoint Formula

The coordinates of the midpoint M of a segment AB are given by ((x₁+x₂)/2, (y₁+y₂)/2).</p
